$comment: Agent execution security, stated by standards/23-agent-execution-security.md (step-budget-bounded, least-privilege-declared) and standards/51-agent-and-tool-execution-prohibitions.md (no-self-modification, retrieved-content-not-instruction); the two forbidden rules were assigned to standard 51 by owner decision of 2026-10-05 (ST-42, #87), which answers Q16 and the standard-field half of Q15. No detector binds here: step-budget-bounded and least-privilege-declared report skipped / not-evaluated; retrieved-content-not-instruction reports prohibited-but-unestablished; no-self-modification is not-evaluable, reports prohibited-but-unestablished and is listed beside the verdict in notEvaluable. The namespace is `agent.` — note MathematicsStandards owns agent.explainable-findings and agent.refusal-on-invariant, which are its own; no id here collides with them.

rules.title: An agent loop carries a step budget
rules.description: Every agent execution loop is bounded by a maximum number of steps or tool calls.
rules.rationale: An unbounded loop is the failure mode that turns a bad plan into an unbounded bill and an unbounded blast radius at the same time.
rules.remediation: Add an explicit step budget and a defined behaviour on exhaustion.

rules.title: Agent credentials are scoped to the tools it declares
rules.description: The credentials an agent holds grant no more than the tools its permission manifest declares.
rules.rationale: An agent that holds a broad credential can reach capabilities nobody enumerated, which means nobody gated them.
rules.remediation: Scope the credential to the declared tool set and record the review.

rules.title: An agent does not modify its own instructions or permissions
rules.description: An agent does not rewrite its own system prompt, tool permissions or step budget during execution.
rules.rationale: An agent that can widen its own authority has no authority bound at all; it has a starting position.
rules.remediation: Establish this through a recorded red-team exercise, not by inspection.
rules.$notEvaluableNote: Static absence of a self-modification code path is not absence of the capability at runtime: an agent with filesystem or configuration tools can reach its own instructions without any code that names them. Establishing this requires a recorded adversarial exercise against the running system, which a separate rule would then examine; no rule in this release does.

rules.title: Retrieved content never acquires instruction authority
rules.description: Content fetched from a retrieval index, a web page or a user document is never treated as instruction.
rules.rationale: This is the injection path that matters most in retrieval systems, because the attacker does not need access to the system — only to something the system will read.
rules.remediation: Isolate untrusted content structurally, and never concatenate it into the instruction channel.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: A system that legitimately needs retrieved content to carry instructions has no trust boundary, which is not a state an exception can approve.
